Yes, if nobody outside your own machine has installed a build. That rule exists only to protect existing users' Accessibility grants, so before launch it costs almost nothing.

- **If anyone has an earlier build:** their Accessibility grant is tied to `is.waiwai.dictation`, so they'd have to re-grant it. Sparkle may also refuse to update across a bundle ID change (I believe it checks this, but verify before relying on it), so they'd need a manual reinstall.
- **Sparkle key:** unaffected. Keep the existing EdDSA key.
- **On your Mac:** run `tccutil reset Accessibility is.waiwai.dictation`, then re-grant to the new build.
- **Also change:** the build setting and Info.plist, anything keyed on the ID (UserDefaults, Keychain, login item), the appcast, and the rules file and `docs/release.md`, so the "permanent" invariant points at the new ID.

I can't see the repo from this session. If you confirm no outside installs, I'd do it now and treat `is.waiwai.openramble` as permanent from launch on.
